purpose: Measure the post-hoc exact-circular-frequency Newtonian amplitude factor proxy against the frozen historical 0.1 versus 0.2 M NQC coefficient stencil comparison at one strong aligned-spin event.
counterfactual: At each saved source state and orbital omega, change only the Newtonian raw-mode amplitude factor by A_proxy = A_raw * (omega_circ_gsl / omega_circ_exact)^(4/3). Form the four amplitude-series differences delta[A, A*q1, A*q2, A*q3], where q1=(pr/(r*omega))^2, q2=q1/r, q3=q1/r^(3/2). Apply their 5-point first- and second-derivative stencils as additive changes to the frozen pilot amplitude derivative rows, and apply the center delta to its frozen captured amplitude values. Retain the saved source targets and all phase-system rows; solve the same NQC equations. Report the resulting 0.1-versus-0.2 coefficient distance only as a post-hoc diagnostic. The original coefficients, 0.026491 historical distance, and failed 0.01 gate remain unchanged.
limitation: The historical centered-DOP853 stencil node states were not serialized. The saved bounded-dense-tight source states are a nearby independent realization of the same captured event; this additive counterfactual does not replay the historical node states exactly and cannot replace the failed historical gate or qualify a release.
